old_title: Polls open after Trump makes last-ditch appeal to midterms voters: Live updates
new_title: Trump 'hiding in private residence' after Republican wipeout: Midterm results live

The polls have opened for Tuesday's crucial midterm elections, during which voters across the country will decide whether Democrats or Republicans will control the U.S. House and Senate.
Democrats are looking to take control of Congress to rebuff President Donald Trump's agenda during the last two years of his term. They will need to flip four seats in the Senate and three seats in the House to receive a majority.
Trump's poor approval rating and Americans' concerns over the high cost of living and war in Iran have been key campaign issues for Democrats.
Many states that Trump previously won are at play in the Senate race, including Alaska, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina, Texas, Kansas and Iowa.
Meanwhile, in the House, Republicans are mostly on the defense, looking to hold on to battleground districts won by Trump in 2024.
The midterms are widely seen as a referendum on Trump's second term. The president made his last-ditch effort to appeal to voters Monday night, calling in to Fox News to urge conservatives to "pretend I'm on the ballot."
Millions will vote in new congressional districts
Millions of Americans are set to vote in new congressional districts this Election Day.
The change comes as a result of redistricting, which has changed the boundaries of about one-third of congressional districts, meaning the congressional map for 2026 looks different than the one used in 2024.
Voting machines down at most polling sites in Westchester County, suburbs north of Manhattan
Voting machines at most polling sites in the suburbs just north of Manhattan were down Tuesday morning due to an issue, officials said.
Scanners at most polling places in Westchester County, New York, began experiencing issues when polls opened at 6 a.m.
Voters are being instructed to stay in line and fill out a paper ballot, which will go into a secure box.
Republican Mike Lawler, who is up for reelection in New York's 17th Congressional District, said every scanner in the county was not working.
His Democratic challenger Cait Conley also posted about the issue, telling voters "don't be dissuaded and have your voice heard."
New York Attorney General Letitia James said her office is looking into the issue.
Midterms Senate poll tracker: Will the Democrats overturn Trump's key majority?
The Democrats' path to victory in the upper chamber of Congress is much tougher but is very much within the realms of possibility.
Paul Farrell has more.
Hillary Clinton says Trump has 'truly lost the plot'
Hillary Clinton had some choice words to share, speaking about Donald Trump during an interview Monday night with CNN's Anderson Cooper.
"He's totally unfettered and unhinged now," Clinton said, referring to how Trump was when he was first elected president in 2016.
"For him to go to the reflecting pool, one of the great failures of his efforts to redo Washington, and stand there as though it was a huge success and go on and on about all his projects, ripping up Washington, destroying the East Wing, building an arch that will interfere with air traffic control navigation in and out of Washington," Clinton said.
"You can't make this up! He is so focused on himself," Clinton exclaimed, later adding, "I mean he's truly lost the plot of being president for the American people, of winning a midterm election."
Midterms House poll tracker: The 10 races you need to know about
Here's a close look at the fight for the House of Representatives, where the Democrats seem all but certain to win back the majority, empowering them to launch investigations into the Trump administration and make the second half of the president's final term much more uncomfortable.
Live: Midterm election polls open after Trump makes final appeal to voters
'Gas prices are high because Trump started a war,' Buttigieg says
Pete Buttigieg, the former transport secretary, presidential contender and mayor of South Bend, Indiana, was on CNN last night with a very clear message to voters about how they got here.
He also had some sharp words for Vice President JD Vance.
Talarico makes appeal to MAGA: 'Let's actually fulfill some of the promise of his political project'
The Texas Senate race between Democrat James Talarico and Republican Ken Paxton will be one of the most eagerly watched this evening.
Here's the former telling conservatives why they should vote for him.
Speaking up for Paxton yesterday was former NBA star Enes Kanter Freedom, who insisted the flailing state attorney general is "actually a very fun guy."
Polls open on East Coast for crucial midterm elections as 56m vote early
The polls opened in Vermont at 5am this morning and have just opened in New Jersey, Virginia, Connecticut and Kentucky too.
According to CNN, around 56 million Americans had already voted by mail before Election Day even dawned.
Early turnout has outpaced the last midterm cycle in 2022 in each of the major Senate battlegrounds, The New York Times notes.
In Texas, for instance, where James Talarico is taking on Ken Paxton, an estimated 7.7 million people have already voted, compared to 5.5 million four years ago, a 41 percent increase.
Early voting is also well up in South Carolina, North Carolina, Michigan, Iowa, Maine, Alaska, Ohio, Georgia and Kansas.

Donald Trump was left to hide out in his private residence at the White House as the midterm results flooded in late on Tuesday, handing his administration a humiliating verdict on the last two years in office.
The Democrats took control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives as voters in conservative bastions shunned Trump's Republican party, with even Texas turning blue after decades of GOP dominance.
"It's very, very dark in the residence," one senior official told The Daily Mail of the mood, as top advisors and allies gathered for a watch party in the East Room. "It's a dark scene."
Another source close to the president told the newspaper that Trump had gone silent by 11 p.m., incensed by the blue wave sweeping away his strongholds.
"He's watching Fox News barely uttering a word and paralysed into silence," the source said, as the president took to social media to blame the network for giving too much airtime to his opponents.
Trump's initial response to the results had been to blame the candidates themselves, before posting a picture of a MAGA-style red hat with "VETO" written on it.
Analysis: Trump's not just a builder now - he's the architect of his own demise
The president's push to solidify the MAGA coalition he rode to victory two years ago led directly to a historic defeat so huge he couldn't even cry fraud, Andrew Feinberg writes.
Watch: Nancy Mace's explodes as she learns of midterms losses
The outgoing South Carolina Republican congresswoman was utterly furious about her party's fate last night.
'Still your President': Trump had such a bad election night that his spokesman had to send a reminder
As Democrats handed Republicans a crushing defeat in the midterms, White House Communications Director Steven Cheung wrote on X: "Donald J. Trump is the President of the United States. Still your President!"
Cheung's post was met with widespread mockery as social media users branded Trump a lame duck.
Rachel Dobkin has the story.
A night of firsts: Historic victories by Black, Native American and LGBTQ+ candidates reshape US politics
A wave of firsts ran alongside the Democratic gains in the 2026 midterms, carrying members of groups long kept largely at the margins into high office across the United States.
The scale of the losses that Democrats inflicted on President Donald Trump will be what the election is first remembered for.
But the results also elevated the country's first Black female governor, the first Native American female governor, the first Native female senator and the first openly gay male U.S. senator.
Here's a closer look.
Who will Democrats pick to run for president in 2028 after midterm elections triumph?
With the dust barely settled on the 2026 midterms, attention is already turning to the next presidential election in two years' time.
New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, California Gov. Gavin Newsom and Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff are just some of the names to have been mentioned so far as Democrats look to the future and the candidate best placed to lead them back to the White House.
Alex Croft asses the possible contenders.
Watch: Jimmy Kimmel compares midterms to Game of Thrones' 'Red Wedding'
Kremlin says it hopes midterm results do not affect Trump's 'peacemaking efforts'
The Kremlin said on Wednesday that it hopes that the results of the US midterm elections will not impact what it said were President Donald Trump's "peacemaking efforts".
In comments broadcast by Russian state media, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said: "We are sincerely counting on (Trump) continuing his peacemaking efforts."
Trump says he will become 'Mr Veto' after losing Congress. But what will he be able to do?
The US president retains the power to block legislation which is likely create deadlock in government, Daniel Keane reports:
Karoline Leavitt makes surprising Trump admission after disastrous midterms for Republicans
Karoline Leavitt conceded that rising gas prices impacted the Republican Party's position in the midterm elections as Democrats secured dramatic victories in the "Blue Tsunami."
The US president had promised low gas prices during his last presidential campaign, insisting costs would come down to $2 a gallon.
However, fuel costs have skyrocketed since Trump joined forces with Israel to attack Iran in February, leading to a collapse in the US president's approval ratings in the weeks leading up to the vote.
Speaking to Fox News, the former White House press secretary said: "Nearly every incumbent president party loses the midterm elections... But I do believe undeniably that the history and the environment was worsened by the prices at the pump."
